[https://stigaview.com/products/win11/v2r7/](https://stigaview.com/products/win11/v2r7/) 

Basically any STIGs that list registry keys as the fix are considered “easy”, since all you have to do is manipulate something in the registry to apply the fix.

You can still (usually) implement STIGs with PowerShell that don’t list registry keys as the fix, but you’ll just need to figure out how to do it.

Also, just because something is already “Passed” as a STIG, doesn’t mean you can’t choose that for a STIG to implement with PowerShell. Just figure out how to “undo” it, then create and test the fix.

For Example:

![][image1]

In the above case, you could simply:

1. enable the guest account  
2. re-scan the machine  
3. observe the STIG failure  
4. figure out how to disable the guest account with PowerShell

Then use that as a STIG implementation toward your internship credit.
